clue.text: Respected English horse touring Middle East

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English

indicators.note: a traveller touring a region goes all round it, so the horse wraps round the Middle East

parts.note: a steed is a horse, split STEE…D round the next piece
ME is the usual abbreviation for the Middle East

explanation.surface: A well-regarded English racehorse on a tour of the Gulf states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Respected English horse' reads as one noun phrase, but the definition stops after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: people who are esteemed are held in high regard.

clue.text: Manager charged with change, Harlow's ending season last in table

indicators.note: something charged with a load carries it
a word's ending is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of Harlow
to alter is to change
one of the four seasons
the team last in a league table sits at its foot, the lowest position

explanation.surface: A football manager charged with turning round a club from Harlow, a town in Essex, that finished the season bottom of the league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged with' tempts you to read W for 'with'; in fact it is Harlow's ending that gets loaded with the change.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Walter Winterbottom was England's first national football manager, from 1946 to 1962.

clue.text: Sound clear and brilliant inside skull — is this needed?

definitions.text: Sound clear and brilliant inside skull — is this needed?

parts.note: the skull is the head, split HEA…D round the rest
A1 = first-rate, with the 1 read as I
a bell rings when it sounds clear

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they need help to make sound ring clear and bright in their head.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition. A1 written AI is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue asks whether you need a device to make sound clear inside your head, which is exactly what a hearing aid does.

clue.text: See 2
More safe crackers triggering alarm?

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, and crazy letters do not stay in order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: Safe-crackers who set off the burglar alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe crackers' reads as one phrase about burglars; split it after 'safe' and 'crackers' becomes the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fearsome frightens people, so it is triggering alarm in them.

clue.text: Neptunian feature regularly seen that spews lava

definitions.text: feature regularly seen that spews lava
definitions.note: the definition is 'feature … that spews lava' with 'regularly seen' as the indicator in the middle

indicators.note: letters seen at regular intervals are every other one

parts.note: the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters: nEpTuNiAn

explanation.surface: An astronomer describes a volcanic feature spotted again and again on Neptune.
explanation.walkthrough: Neptune is a red herring: the volcano is in Sicily, and the 'feature' is read with the words around the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Etna, on Sicily, is Europe's most active volcano, a landscape feature that erupts lava.

clue.text: World's response where Conservative rises

indicators.note: in a down entry, something that rises moves towards the top

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a reaction is a response; lift its C out, leaving REATION

explanation.surface: A commentator reports how the world reacted when the Conservatives surged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'World's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is 'is': World is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym by sense: creation is everything that was created, the whole world.

clue.text: See 2
Room tiny arachnid enters backwards — it has four dimensions

indicators.note: to enter a room is to go inside it

parts.note: room and space both mean extent to move in, split SPAC…E

indicators.note: the arachnid's letters run the other way

parts.note: a mite is a tiny eight-legged creature

explanation.surface: A mite creeps into a room, followed by a note that the room has four dimensions.
explanation.walkthrough: Three dimensions of space plus one of time make the four; ordinary rooms have only three.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: in relativity, space-time is one continuum of three space dimensions and one of time.

clue.text: Strange sort of force leaving dismembered body

indicators.note: strange means out of the ordinary, so SORT comes out of its usual order
F, for force, leaves 'of'

parts.note: anagram fodder
'of' with F (force, the physics symbol) removed

explanation.surface: A detective sees a strange kind of force at work in the remains of a dismembered body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of force' looks like a physics term; the force is only an F to be taken out of 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a torso is the trunk left when a body has lost its head and limbs.

clue.text: Metallica finally exiting festival compound

indicators.note: what comes finally in Metallica is its last letter

parts.note: the Christian spring festival

indicators.note: a letter exiting a word goes out of it, so the A leaves

parts.note: last letter of Metallica, removed from EASTER

explanation.surface: The heavy metal band Metallica pulls out of a music festival at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Festival' looks like a rock festival; it is the church one.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemistry sense: an ester is a compound formed when an acid reacts with an alcohol.

clue.text: Brawling woman to call Turkish leader, not without guts

parts.note: to term something is to call it that
an aga was an Ottoman commander

indicators.note: a gutted word has lost its insides, so NOT keeps only N and T

parts.note: NOT emptied

explanation.surface: A pugnacious woman refuses to address a Turkish chief as anything but gutless.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA, an Ottoman title, is a crossword staple for 'Turkish leader'.
explanation.definitionFit: Termagant was once a supposed Muslim deity played as a ranting tyrant in medieval plays, and the name passed to any violent, quarrelsome woman.

clue.text: Sailor runs into sea, extremely eager

indicators.note: running into the sea puts the runs inside it

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea, split MA…IN
R = runs, the cricket scoring abbreviation

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of eager

explanation.surface: An eager sailor dashes into the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the high seas, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: mariner, from Latin mare 'sea', is a formal word for a seafarer.

clue.text: Mansion rebuilt for personal pleasure

indicators.note: a rebuilt house is put together again differently, and so are the letters

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A rich owner remodels a stately home just to please themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Personal pleasure' sounds like a hobby; it is a coy euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism: onanism is masturbation, pleasure a person gives themselves.

clue.text: Supremely evil influence in Chartist reforms

indicators.note: to re-form something is to shape it anew, so the letters take a new shape

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A historian blames a wicked influence for the Chartists' reform programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chartists were a 19th-century British movement for voting reform, which is why 'reforms' fits the surface. 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian belief the Antichrist is Christ's great adversary, the embodiment of evil at the end of days.

clue.text: American rotter holding Henry back in Russian cottage

indicators.note: the American rotter holds Henry inside
going back means reading the letters from the end

parts.note: A = American
H = henry, the unit of inductance
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: An American scoundrel keeps a man named Henry captive in a Russian country house.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry is the unit of inductance, not a man; the whole string is turned round at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A loanword: dacha is the Russian word for a country house or summer cottage outside a city.

clue.text: Dish with seafood: chicken to follow

parts.note: a cock is a male chicken
to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A menu: a seafood starter, with chicken as the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: A prawn cocktail is a classic British starter of prawns in a pink sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a seafood cocktail, such as prawn cocktail, is shellfish served cold in a sauce.

clue.text: Proper contest shortened

indicators.note: a shortened word loses its tail, here the final L

parts.note: a duel is a contest between two, less its last letter

explanation.surface: A proper contest cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proper contest' reads as one phrase; the first word alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in use: 'with due care' means with proper care, what is fitting.

clue.text: Kid arrested by police inspector, put away for attack

parts.note: DI = Detective Inspector
to put food away is to eat it, split AT…E
to kid or rib is to tease

explanation.surface: A youngster is arrested by a detective and jailed for assault.
explanation.walkthrough: Kid is the verb 'tease', not a child, and put away means eaten, not jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A verbal sense: a diatribe is a bitter spoken or written attack.

clue.text: End of sunbathing? Make tracks for dance

parts.note: a tan is the end product of sunbathing
to make tracks is to leave

explanation.surface: Sunbathing over, it is time to head off to a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of sunbathing' looks like a last letter, G; the question mark says it is the end in the sense of result.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the tango, from Buenos Aires, is one kind of ballroom dance.

clue.text: Insider from Acton wrongly claiming prize

indicators.note: letters put wrongly are out of their right order

parts.note: anagram fodder, split OC…ANT round CUP
a trophy cup is a prize

explanation.surface: An insider from Acton, a district of west London, falsely claims a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' looks like a hidden-word or source instruction but is only surface glue for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic-leaning synonym: an occupant is literally someone inside a building or vehicle.

clue.text: Atlantic Provinces bordering right rural idyll

parts.note: Acadia was the French colony in what are now Canada's Maritime provinces, split A…CADIA
R = right

explanation.surface: Canada's Atlantic seaboard presented as an unspoilt countryside paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: Acadia is the historical name for the French lands of Canada's Atlantic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary sense: Arcadia, a region of Greece, stands in pastoral poetry for an idyllic countryside.

clue.text: Cold in HGV in polar region

parts.note: an HGV (heavy goods vehicle) is a lorry; an artic is an articulated one, split AR…TIC
C = cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A lorry driver feels the cold in a polar landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: Artic is British slang for an articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper name by description: the Arctic is the region round the North Pole.

clue.text: Short French article perhaps coming to a point?

parts.note: la is French for 'the', feminine
a cone comes to a point

explanation.surface: A short article in French that gets straight to the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short … coming to a point' sounds like one description of terse writing; the question mark marks the playful reading of CONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spartans of Laconia were famous for curt speech, so laconic means short in words.

clue.text: Secure gold in horse-drawn carriage

parts.note: to land a deal is to secure it
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Bullion being shipped safely in a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container instruction but is a link word; the pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by type: the landau, named after the German town of Landau, is a four-wheeled carriage with a folding top.

clue.text: Drink downed noisily at bar after opening

indicators.note: only the letters of bar after its first
said noisily means said out loud, so we take the sound of the word

parts.note: to neck a drink is to down it
bar without its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone gulps a drink loudly at the pub bar as soon as it opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neck' is British slang for drinking fast.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth nectar is the drink of the gods, and by extension any delicious drink.

clue.text: Vessel crossing river in southwest — atomic boat

parts.note: a can is a metal container, split CA…N
the Tamar divides Devon and Cornwall in England's southwest
A = atomic, as in A-bomb

explanation.surface: A ship steams across a river in the West Country, followed by a nuclear-powered boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' looks like the definition for a boat; it is the container, and the boat comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by type: a catamaran is a boat with twin parallel hulls.

clue.text: Sheep's flesh not being cooked for dog

indicators.note: food being cooked is 'on'; not so, ON goes

parts.note: mutton is the meat of a sheep, less ON

explanation.surface: Raw mutton handed to the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Food on the stove is 'on', so meat that is not being cooked loses ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal usage: mutt is a slangy word for a dog, especially a mongrel.

clue.text: State main points again where MP bans duke

indicators.note: to ban someone is to keep them out

parts.note: a redcap is a British military policeman, from the red cap band
D = duke, removed

explanation.surface: A summary of a debate where a Member of Parliament shuts out a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: MP looks like Member of Parliament; it is Military Police, whose British nickname is redcaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Recap is short for recapitulate, to go over the main points once more.

clue.text: Tees had the ne plus ultra, ensnaring old fool

parts.note: Tees is the setter, so 'Tees had' is I'D

indicators.note: a snare traps its prey inside, so the ultimate traps the old

parts.note: the ultimate is 'it', split I…T
O = old

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of having the very best, except that it trapped an old fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Ne plus ultra is Latin for 'nothing further', the ultimate; that is 'it', as in 'this is it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: idiot, from Greek for a private, ignorant person, now just means a fool.

clue.text: Seaman stole this empty wagon

parts.note: a boa is a feathery stole

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, so THIS keeps only T and S

parts.note: THIS emptied
a wain is an old farm wagon

explanation.surface: A sailor stole this cart after emptying it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' reads as a verb, the seaman's theft; it is the noun, a scarf-like wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank by type: the boatswain, or bosun, is the ship's officer in charge of crew and rigging.
